opportunities.name: Research paper lookup: arXiv search → Semantic Scholar citations → log to Notes
opportunities.description: For a given topic, subject category and year, find the newest matching paper with arXiv Advanced Search, look up its citation count on Semantic Scholar, and add a note in the form 'topic (year): title by first author, N citations'.
steps: Open arxiv.org and click Search, then go to Advanced Search
Type the topic into the search term field (field: Title)
Tick the subject category checkbox
Select 'Specific year' and type the year
Click Search and take the first result's title and first author
Open semanticscholar.org, reject cookies if asked, and paste the paper title into the search box
Search and read the citation count on the matching result
Open Notes, click 'New note' and type '<topic> (<year>): <title> by <first author>, <N> citations'

instances.values: topic=retrieval augmented generation; subject=Computer Science; year=2023 → RIGHT: Retrieval-augmented Generation for Mainstream Hashtag Recommendation, Run-Ze Fan, 11 citations
topic=protein structure diffusion; subject=Quantitative Biology; year=2024 → Accelerating Inference in Molecular Diffusion Models..., Ian Dunn, 7 citations

opportunities.name: Legal case lookup: CourtListener case → LII statute → log to Notes
opportunities.description: For a given Supreme Court case and related statute, find the case's citation and decision date on CourtListener, look up the statute's section title on Cornell LII, and add a note in the form 'Case: citation, decided date. See statute (section title)'.
steps: Open CourtListener and go to Case Law > Search Case Law
Type the case name into the keyword search and click Search
Open the Supreme Court opinion in the results and note its U.S. Reports citation and decision date
Open LII (law.cornell.edu) and type the statute citation (e.g. '18 U.S.C. 2703') into the search box
Read the section title on the first result
Open Notes, click 'New note' and type '<case>: <citation>, decided <date>. See <statute> (<section title>)'

opportunities.name: Event planning: Peerspace venue search → 1800flowers flowers → email summary
opportunities.description: For a given event type and city, search Peerspace for a venue, search 1800flowers for flowers, and draft an email to the organizer that summarizes venue, catering and flower options.
steps: Open peerspace.com and type the event type into 'What are you planning?'
Type the city into 'Where?' and pick it from the autocomplete list
Click Search and look at the venue results (or the 'not recognized' message)
Open 1800flowers.com, decline cookies, and search for the flower type
Write down the first suitable product and its price
Open New message, enter the recipient, a subject like '<event> on <date>: venue, food, flowers' and a body that summarizes what was found
Send or discard the draft
